paper_title: The Unseen Targets of Hate -- A Systematic Review of Hateful   Communication Datasets
caption: : Linguistic and geographic trends over time in harmful language research. Notably, the number of datasets for the non-top five languages continues to be lower than all English ones, while since 2017 we see more and more datasets in languages other than English.
model_annotation: This grouped vertical bar chart illustrates the number of datasets published per year, categorized by language. The horizontal category axis is labeled "Year" and displays distinct years sorted chronologically from 2012 to 2022. The vertical value axis is labeled "Number of datasets" and utilizes a logarithmic scale, featuring major tick marks and corresponding horizontal grid lines at intervals of $10^0$, $10^1$, and $10^2$. Within each year, data is represented by a clustered group of vertical bars, where each bar's color corresponds to a specific language category defined in the legend: English (blue), All other (orange), Arabic (green), Bengali (red), Spanish (purple), and Russian (brown). The bars within each group are arranged side-by-side in the exact order of the legend. From 2012 to 2015, only the English category is present, showing values of approximately 2 in 2012 and 2013, and 3 in 2014 and 2015. Beginning in 2016, the "All other" category is introduced at roughly 3 datasets, while English reaches 10. Over subsequent years, the groups expand to include additional languages. The tallest bar on the chart belongs to English in 2021, representing an approximate value of 90, and is clustered with "All other" (~35), Arabic (~15), Bengali (~14), Spanish (~11), and Russian (~9). The shortest bars align with the $10^0$ (or 1) line, seen for Bengali in 2017 and 2018, and Russian in 2022. Visually, the bars for the final category on the x-axis, 2022, are emphasized differently than the rest of the chart, rendered in lighter, semi-transparent shades of the respective legend colors, while all bars from 2012 to 2021 are solid and opaque.
